title: Independent set algorithms from tropical circuit size
formal: Do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\), a real constant \(K>0\) and an integer \(a\ge1\) such that, for every finite simple graph \(G\) on \(n\ge1\) labeled vertices and every nonnegative integer weight vector \(w\), the machine outputs the exact value \(\operatorname{MWIS}(G,w)\) within \(K(\tau(G)+n+L+1)^a\) bit operations? Here \(L\) is the total encoded length of the weights and \(\tau(G)\) is the minimum tropical-circuit size defined below. The input contains only \(G,w\), without a circuit, a decomposition or the value of \(\tau(G)\).
definitions:
The vertex set is \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The graph is supplied as \(n\) in binary and its explicit \(n\times n\) symmetric zero-diagonal binary adjacency matrix. The weights \(w_1,\ldots,w_n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) are listed in binary with delimiters, including one zero bit for a zero weight. Let \(L\) include all those weight bits and delimiters. A set \(I\subseteq[n]\) is independent if no two distinct vertices of \(I\) are adjacent. For every real vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
\operatorname{MWIS}(G,x)=\max_{\substack{I\subseteq[n]\\ I\text{ independent}}}\ \sum_{v\in I}x_v.
\]
The empty set is allowed and has weight zero. The required output of \(A\) is the nonnegative integer \(\operatorname{MWIS}(G,w)\), in ordinary binary notation.

A tropical circuit on variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is a finite directed acyclic graph with one designated output gate. Each input gate has no incoming wires and is labeled by one variable or by the constant \(0\). Every other gate has two input wires and is labeled either \(\max\) or \(+\), interpreted as ordinary maximum or addition of real numbers. Input wires may carry the same previously computed value; fan-out is unrestricted. No other constants, comparisons with branching, multiplication, subtraction or oracle gates are allowed. Size is the total number of gates, including input and constant gates. A circuit for \(G\) is valid if its output equals \(\operatorname{MWIS}(G,x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n\). Its topology and labels depend on \(G\) alone, not on the weight assignment. Define \(\tau(G)\) as the minimum size of such a valid circuit. This finite integer exists for every graph.

The machine \(A\) may perform arbitrary deterministic Turing-machine computation; it is not restricted to the operations allowed in the circuits that define \(\tau\). Its program and the constants \(K,a\) are independent of \(G,w,n\). All graph reads, arithmetic on binary weights, preprocessing and output writing are charged. The \(n\) term in a fixed polynomial also accounts for the \(n^2\)-bit adjacency matrix. There are no random bits, nonuniform advice or uncharged preprocessing. The guarantee is a worst-case bound for each valid input. Only the optimum value is requested, not a witnessing independent set or a tropical circuit.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of a uniform algorithm and fixed constants meeting the exact computational task and bound for all graphs and weights, or a complete Lean proof of their nonexistence. A quasipolynomial dependence on the circuit-size parameter, a construction that is supplied a circuit, or an algorithm restricted to a graph class does not establish the stated polynomial target. A conditional lower bound retains its condition and alone does not give an unconditional negative answer.
why: A compact circuit can express a dynamic program for every weight assignment to one graph without explaining how to discover it. This question asks whether the existence of that compact representation always yields an effective uniform algorithm, connecting nonuniform computation with exact graph optimization.

importance.reason: A general algorithm-versus-representation question connecting graph structure, dynamic programming and automatization beyond one decomposition family.

context_blocks.text: The author’s current problem list asks for polynomial or quasipolynomial running time in the smallest circuit size. This card retains its previously selected polynomial branch and exact value output; it does not require constructing a circuit. The binary model makes weight arithmetic part of the cost.

The paper defines the circuit parameter using all real weights. The card retains its approved nonnegative-weight convention. Section 2.2 observes that these conventions have linearly related circuit sizes, so they give the same polynomial-automatization question.

Corollary 4 establishes polynomial-overhead circuit construction for bounded-degree graphs and for graphs excluding a fixed minor. The unrestricted graph class is the remaining scope of the author’s question.

The paper’s lower bounds on tropical circuits do not themselves lower-bound an unrestricted algorithm given the graph and weights. The target concerns how quickly that algorithm can exploit small circuit complexity, rather than requiring its computation to use only maximum and addition.

sentences: A tropical circuit combines vertex weights using only maximum and addition.
For each graph, its minimum circuit size measures how compactly maximum independent-set weight can be represented for every nonnegative weight assignment.
The question asks for one deterministic algorithm whose bit cost is polynomial in that circuit size and the input parameters.
The algorithm receives only the graph and weights, and may use unrestricted computation to output the exact optimum value.
The known construction for restricted graph classes leaves the author’s general polynomial-automatization question open in the sources checked.
